## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Catukkapuggalapaññatti* is a major section of the *Puggalapaññatti*, the third or fourth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Following the mātikā framework outlined in the *Catukkauddesa* (Pp 1.4), the text provides comprehensive analytical definitions of persons classified into fourfold groupings [SuttaCentral]. Two modern translations across two languages are registered on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
The work shares an extensive body of doctrinal material with the Sutta Piṭaka, drawing directly on discourses from the *Catukkanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral identifies specific thematic and textual parallels or citations in numerous fourfold suttas, including the *Tamotamasutta* (AN 4.85), *Potaliyasutta* (AN 4.100), *Paṭhamavalāhakasutta* (AN 4.101), *Kumbhasutta* (AN 4.103), *Udakarahadasutta* (AN 4.104), *Ambasutta* (AN 4.105), *Balībaddasutta* (AN 4.108), *Rukkhasutta* (AN 4.109), *Āsīvisasutta* (AN 4.110), *Paṭhamanānākaraṇasutta* (AN 4.123), *Ugghaṭitaññūsutta* (AN 4.133), *Uṭṭhānaphalasutta* (AN 4.134), *Sāvajjasutta* (AN 4.135), *Dhammakathikasutta* (AN 4.139), and *Sikkhāpadasutta* (AN 4.201), alongside mentions in AN 3.116, the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 13.7), the *Petakopadesa* (Pe 8), and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [SuttaCentral].
Automated analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this close canonical integration, identifying over 2,100 shared passages between the *Catukkapuggalapaññatti* and the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), with major correspondences such as §110.1–125.4 aligned with AN 4.198 [DharmaNexus]. Significant internal reuse is also detected with other Aṅguttara divisions (AN 3, AN 5, AN 8, AN 10), the *Dīgha Nikāya* (DN 2), the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 27, MN 51, MN 94, MN 101), and other sections of the *Puggalapaññatti* itself (Pp 2.1, Pp 2.2, Pp 2.3) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with Chinese Āgama collections (*Madhyama Āgama*, T 26; *Ekottarika Āgama*, T 125), Sanskrit treatises including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, *Saṅghabhedavastu*, *Mahāvastu*, and the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, and Tibetan canonical texts including the *Vinayavastu* and various Prajñāpāramitā scriptures [DharmaNexus].
